texts.orig: Q: How do you think about setting goals for your team (and company)?
texts.text: Q: How do you think about setting goals for your team (and company)?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As a leader, one of your
texts.text: As a leader, one of your

texts.label: text
texts.orig: most important
texts.text: most important

texts.label: text
texts.orig: jobs is to make sure everyone is moving in the same direction — channeling all of their energy, focus, and resources towards the same outcome.
texts.text: jobs is to make sure everyone is moving in the same direction — channeling all of their energy, focus, and resources towards the same outcome.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: That's exactly what goals are for.
texts.text: That's exactly what goals are for.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Goals are a tool to help you align and motivate everyone on your team to successfully achieve a desired outcome. Below, I share a framework that I’ve used to set goals and institute them across an organization.
texts.text: Goals are a tool to help you align and motivate everyone on your team to successfully achieve a desired outcome. Below, I share a framework that I’ve used to set goals and institute them across an organization.

texts.orig: Why set goals?

texts.orig: Let’s start by thinking about where goals fit into the bigger picture:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Goals have three primary benefits:
texts.text: Goals have three primary benefits:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Clarity
texts.text: Clarity

texts.label: text

texts.text: : You know what success looks like

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Alignment

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : All team members know what success looks like

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Motivation
texts.text: Motivation

texts.label: text

texts.text: : A push to achieve more than you would have otherwise

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I want to highlight one of the biggest traps I see leaders fall into: assuming that everyone on their team is aligned on what success looks like. The metaphor I like to use for this (inspired by a former colleague) is a silver burrito. Like the ones you see on the Chipotle billboards:
texts.text: I want to highlight one of the biggest traps I see leaders fall into: assuming that everyone on their team is aligned on what success looks like. The metaphor I like to use for this (inspired by a former colleague) is a silver burrito. Like the ones you see on the Chipotle billboards:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: That burrito looks delicious because we’re all picturing our favorite burrito inside the silver wrapping. Yum! Similarly, projects often look delicious to team members because they're each imagining different goals — goals that they are personally most excited about (e.g. increase conversion vs. make users happier vs. refactoring code).
texts.text: That burrito looks delicious because we’re all picturing our favorite burrito inside the silver wrapping. Yum! Similarly, projects often look delicious to team members because they're each imagining different goals — goals that they are personally most excited about (e.g. increase conversion vs. make users happier vs. refactoring code).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A product leader’s job is to unwrap the burrito and make sure everyone is seeing the same thing.
texts.text: A product leader’s job is to unwrap the burrito and make sure everyone is seeing the same thing.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Let’s talk about how to do that.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: How to set goals
texts.text: How to set goals

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Now that we know a goal is just a way to understand whether you’re achieving your strategy, let’s talk about how to decide what the actual goal should be.
texts.text: Now that we know a goal is just a way to understand whether you’re achieving your strategy, let’s talk about how to decide what the actual goal should be.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A good goal has the following attributes:
texts.text: A good goal has the following attributes:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Simple
texts.text: Simple

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : Everyone understands what it is and how it’s measured
texts.text: : Everyone understands what it is and how it’s measured

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Concrete
texts.text: Concrete

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : It’s obvious if you've achieved it
texts.text: : It’s obvious if you've achieved it

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Worthwhile
texts.text: Worthwhile

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : Making an impact actually matters to the business
texts.text: : Making an impact actually matters to the business

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Stable
texts.text: Stable

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : You’re confident your work won’t be drowned out by noise
texts.text: : You’re confident your work won’t be drowned out by noise

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Quick feedback loop
texts.text: Quick feedback loop

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : Changes in the product can quickly be seen in the metric
texts.text: : Changes in the product can quickly be seen in the metric

texts.label: text
texts.orig: With these attributes in mind, next let's focus on defining your goal, which includes two parts: (1) picking the metric, and (2) deciding much you want to move it.
texts.text: With these attributes in mind, next let's focus on defining your goal, which includes two parts: (1) picking the metric, and (2) deciding much you want to move it.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 1. Pick the metric
texts.text: 1. Pick the metric

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Start with your business’

texts.label: text
texts.orig: north star metric
texts.text: north star metric

texts.label: text
texts.orig: —whether it’s revenue, subscriptions, or media consumed— and figure out what set of levers move that metric.
texts.text: —whether it’s revenue, subscriptions, or media consumed— and figure out what set of levers move that metric.

texts.orig: For example, at Airbnb our north star metric was

texts.label: text

texts.label: text
texts.orig: . The levers that moved this metric were loosely broken up into demand, supply, and the dynamics between the two. One level deeper, on say demand, we looked at things like site visits, conversion, and cancellation rate.
texts.text: . The levers that moved this metric were loosely broken up into demand, supply, and the dynamics between the two. One level deeper, on say demand, we looked at things like site visits, conversion, and cancellation rate.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This combination of levers is often referred to as a company’s growth model. When you do this right, all of the levers add up to 100% of what drives the business, and helps you understand where your biggest opportunities are. Essentially, it’s the math formula of the business.
texts.text: This combination of levers is often referred to as a company’s growth model. When you do this right, all of the levers add up to 100% of what drives the business, and helps you understand where your biggest opportunities are. Essentially, it’s the math formula of the business.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: With this collection of levers, figure out which of those levers present the largest constraint (or bottleneck) for your business.
texts.text: With this collection of levers, figure out which of those levers present the largest constraint (or bottleneck) for your business.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Ask yourself: what’s the one thing that, if moved, would unlock the most growth?
texts.text: Ask yourself: what’s the one thing that, if moved, would unlock the most growth?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Finally, determine the best concrete metric to track that lever. For instance, at Airbnb, after we determined that homes (aka supply) was our primary constraint to growth, we built a team focused just on growing supply. Our metric was "New listings that received at least one booking."
texts.text: Finally, determine the best concrete metric to track that lever. For instance, at Airbnb, after we determined that homes (aka supply) was our primary constraint to growth, we built a team focused just on growing supply. Our metric was "New listings that received at least one booking."

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 2. Pick the threshold (aka the goal)
texts.text: 2. Pick the threshold (aka the goal)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: With your metric set, landing on the right threshold for that metric (aka your goal) requires a combination of tops-down and bottoms-up thinking.
texts.text: With your metric set, landing on the right threshold for that metric (aka your goal) requires a combination of tops-down and bottoms-up thinking.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Tops-down
texts.text: Tops-down

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : In order for your business to achieve the ideal level of growth required for long-term success, how much does this metric need to move?
texts.text: : In order for your business to achieve the ideal level of growth required for long-term success, how much does this metric need to move?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Bottoms-up
texts.text: Bottoms-up

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : Knowing what you know today, what impact could your team realistically deliver with current resources (or, with some increase in resources)?
texts.text: : Knowing what you know today, what impact could your team realistically deliver with current resources (or, with some increase in resources)?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your resulting number usually ends up being somewhere in the middle, and adjusted for resources you end getting.
texts.text: Your resulting number usually ends up being somewhere in the middle, and adjusted for resources you end getting.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I often get asked just how ambitious leaders should be when setting goals. I think about a goal like a video game. Video games are built to ensure that the next level is
texts.text: I often get asked just how ambitious leaders should be when setting goals. I think about a goal like a video game. Video games are built to ensure that the next level is

texts.label: text
texts.orig: just
texts.text: just

texts.label: text
texts.orig: hard enough to motivate you to continue, but not so hard that you give up. You want to win—even if it’s tough—and victory always seems just within reach. But when it feels impossible, you quickly give up.
texts.text: hard enough to motivate you to continue, but not so hard that you give up. You want to win—even if it’s tough—and victory always seems just within reach. But when it feels impossible, you quickly give up.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: So when setting a goal, just like in a video game, you want your goal to motivate your team to push beyond what's comfortable, but never make it feel impossible. Brian Chesky (CEO of Airbnb) liked to say that goals should feel “uncomfortable, but not impossible.”

texts.orig: How to use goals once you have them

texts.label: text
texts.orig: You’ve done the hard work to set a concrete goal that’s aligned with your mission and vision. But now that you have a goal, what the heck do you do with it?
texts.text: You’ve done the hard work to set a concrete goal that’s aligned with your mission and vision. But now that you have a goal, what the heck do you do with it?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Get buy-in:
texts.text: Get buy-in:

texts.label: text

texts.text: Make sure everyone on your team (as well as the folks above), buy into it.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Instrument:
texts.text: Instrument:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Implement a tool that allows your team to easily watch this metric. Build a dashboard that’s accessible and easy to find. Triple-check the data is valid.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Prioritize:
texts.text: Prioritize:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Decide what to prioritize based on what will have the most impact on your goal. With alignment on what success looks like across the team, decisions that felt hard before should be much easier.
texts.text: Decide what to prioritize based on what will have the most impact on your goal. With alignment on what success looks like across the team, decisions that felt hard before should be much easier.

texts.orig: Operationalize:
texts.text: Operationalize:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Build this metric into your team workflows. Find a cadence of checking in on this metric individually with your team, and with management. Share progress on the goal frequently.
texts.text: Build this metric into your team workflows. Find a cadence of checking in on this metric individually with your team, and with management. Share progress on the goal frequently.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Revisit:
texts.text: Revisit:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As you continue to monitor your metric (and how your work is impacting it), you might conclude that something just isn’t right. Give yourself an opportunity to revisit the goal. Consider whether it still meets the broader attributes and if your team actually has the ability to move it.
